paragraphs: A ring crane does not stand on outriggers, it stands on a circular track, and that is why it can lift what nothing else can. The load is spread around the ring instead of being fought by counterweight alone, which is how refinery vessels and reactor components get placed at all.
The model holds 599,443 polygons and 692,025 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, suited to the heavily repeated lattice structure. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $129 it suits heavy industry and construction visualisation, equipment marketing, logistics and engineering presentation, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.

The Cabri G2 is a training helicopter designed by an engineer who had worked on far larger machines and wanted the small end done properly. A composite airframe, a shrouded tail rotor and energy absorbing seats put safety features into a two seater that used to be reserved for airliners.

The airframe holds 496,082 polygons and 507,314 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 27 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits aviation training visualisation, flight simulation, general aviation marketing, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

The Prelude name belongs to a period when Honda made coupes for people who wanted a sports car that could be driven every day. Bringing it back as a Type R puts it in the company's most serious performance line, which is a very different proposition from where the badge started.
The model holds 174,534 polygons and 187,710 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, finished in white, and carries StemCell certification.
At $129 it suits automotive marketing and configurators, street and architectural scenes, advertising, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The abaya is cut to fall from the shoulders and nowhere else, and wide sleeves are what give it movement. A hooded version removes the need for a separate headcovering, which changes both the silhouette and how the garment is actually worn.
The garment holds 23,821 polygons and 23,889 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in green, and is supplied as a static piece. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $129 it suits fashion and garment visualisation, retail and e-commerce imagery, cultural and editorial illustration, advertising, film costume and game characters. On sale since 2025.

An eagle in the strike is all talons and no wing. The wings come back and up to brake, the feet come forward, and for a fraction of a second the bird is a completely different shape from the one people picture when they think of an eagle in flight.
The model holds 33,037 polygons and 67,048 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in the attacking pose. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $129 it suits wildlife and nature visualisation, heraldic and emblematic imagery, documentary and education work, game creatures, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The bulk bag is one of the quietest pieces of industrial design there is: a woven sack with lifting loops that moves a tonne of anything granular and then folds flat. Paired with a small crane, it is how most powders and aggregates actually get around a site.
The model holds 104,743 polygons and 107,886 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the crane together with the bag, and carries StemCell certification.
At $129 it suits industrial and logistics visualisation, materials handling presentation, training and safety material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The MCI coach is the shape of long distance travel in North America. Luggage under the floor, a high floor cabin above it, and a body designed for a driver who will be behind the wheel for eight hours rather than for a city route with a stop every block.

The model holds 259,457 polygons and 274,608 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 26 maps, 3 at 8192x8192, 11 at 4096x4096, 10 at 2048x2048, one at 1024x1024 and one at 512x512. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits transport and travel visualisation, fleet and livery mockups, street and architectural scenes, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2017.

The LT was International's attempt to win back long haul drivers with aerodynamics rather than chrome. Every panel is shaped for fuel economy, and the argument to an owner operator is straightforward: the shape pays for itself over a million miles.

The model holds 260,918 polygons and 290,107 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 8 maps, 7 at 4096x4096 and one at 2048x2048, and comes rigged. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $129 it suits transport and logistics visualisation, haulage marketing, fleet mockups, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

The A330 has quietly outlived most of its contemporaries by being the right size for routes that are too long for a narrow body and too thin for anything larger. Cathay Pacific built much of its regional network on exactly that gap.

The airframe is light at 78,514 polygons and 85,228 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps, 3 of them at 8192x8192 and 9 at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits flight simulation, airline and airport visualisation, travel advertising, film backgrounds and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

The Do 31 is the only jet transport ever built that could take off vertically, and it remains so. Lift engines in pods on the wingtips, cruise engines that vectored their thrust, and a programme cancelled because the fuel cost of hovering a cargo aircraft turned out to be exactly as bad as feared.

The airframe holds 127,277 polygons and 133,180 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 16 maps, 8 at 4096x4096 and 8 at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits aviation history and documentary work, museum and exhibition material, flight simulation, film and game environments. On sale since 2015.

The Templars were a banking order that happened to fight, and the white surcoat with its cross was a uniform in an age that had almost none. It is one of the few medieval costumes recognisable to people who know nothing else about the period.

The figure holds 34,036 polygons and 35,733 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 19 maps all at 4096x4096, and is supplied in a T pose ready for your own rig. It carries StemCell certification, and a walking pose is offered separately.
At $129 it suits game characters, historical and fantasy film work, education and museum material, tabletop illustration and previsualisation. On sale since 2020.

The Bell 47 is the helicopter with the goldfish bowl cockpit and the exposed lattice tail, and it is in the design collection of the Museum of Modern Art for exactly that honesty of construction. It was the first helicopter certified for civil use anywhere.

The airframe holds 144,385 polygons and 154,424 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 9 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and the library also holds a red scheme and rigged builds of both.
At $129 it suits aviation history and documentary work, museum and exhibition material, period film and television, flight simulation and game environments. On sale since 2017.

The Abrams runs a gas turbine, which is why it sounds like an aircraft and drinks like one. Everything else about the tank is a compromise around composite armour thick enough to justify the weight, and the silhouette has barely changed in four decades of upgrades.

The model holds 479,236 polygons and 486,010 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps, 4 at 8192x8192, 7 at 4096x4096, one at 2048x2048 and one at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits defence visualisation and presentation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, film and television, and game environments. On sale since 2016.

The Mark V was built to deliver small teams a long way, fast, and to leave again before anyone worked out it had been there. It is a boat designed around a schedule rather than a fight, which is why speed and range beat armament in every decision on it.
The model holds 187,273 polygons and 195,386 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification. Dark and light camouflage builds are offered separately.
At $129 it suits military and naval visualisation, defence presentation, documentary and film, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.
